prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"I want to try a new red wine that tastes like pepper and nuts. Can you find me something good between 20 and 40 euros?"

List A:
Wine 1: Red Blend, Italy, $13. Tasting note: "This screwcap red blend from northern Italy offers a fantastic little package at a very attractive low price. Pristine aromas of red berry and white cherry are offset by subtle shadings of sweet spice and crushed mineral. The wine drinks very well."
Wine 2: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $12. Tasting note: "This is a soft wine, lightly spicy and toasty. With its stalky red fruits and gentle tannins, it is an easy wine to drink with its young fruit and crunchy aftertaste."
Wine 3: Zweigelt, Austria, $18. Tasting note: "Cherry, sage, blackberry and white pepper mingle to make a refreshing and rounded wine ideal for uncomplicated pleasure. Drink now, preferably with canapés or a light lunch where its beautiful and resonant aftertaste of red cherry will impress."
Wine 4: Red Blend, US, $27. Tasting note: "Spiced meats, cherry and pepper give this plucky red a food-friendly edge. On the palate, it's spicy and slightly tart, with cranberry, blueberry and crushed herbs. Earthy and dry, the wine will pair well with spiced meat and pastas."
Wine 5: Gamay, France, $22. Tasting note: "Now fully mature, this soft wine has berry flavors over a dry core. It is rich with a touch of pepper and jammy red fruitiness leading to a toasty aftertaste. Drink now."

List B:
Wine 1: Syrah, US, $18. Tasting note: "A remarkable wine for under $20, well made and varietally defined in cinnamon, white pepper and gamy red fruit."
Wine 2: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $11. Tasting note: "Harsh and sharp in tannins and acids, but this is a pretty good price for a dry, full-bodied red wine with blackberry and currant flavors. Drink with rustic fare, such as burgers or pasta with sausages."
Wine 3: Cabernet Sauvignon, France, $8. Tasting note: "This wine is quite the bargain, offering nice fruit and spice for under $10. Simply structured with soft tannins, juicy black currant and plum flavors all accented by a hint of pepper. Drink now."
Wine 4: Rosé, France, $17. Tasting note: "This attractively crisp wine packed with red berry fruits is light and lively. It offers plenty of acidity along with a touch of pepper and cinnamon. Drink now."
Wine 5: Zweigelt, Austria, price unknown. Tasting note: "A simple wine full of red cherry flavors on the nose and palate, with an enticing white pepper edge that makes it very refreshing. This could be chilled and is an ideal, lighter-style red for informal entertainment."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
